messages.author: 05f88d7a80e7066c
messages.subject: R crashed: terminate called after throwing an instance of 'affymetrix_calvin_exceptions::UnableToOpenFileException'
parts:
Hello,

I am a beginner of exon array analysis and
aroma.affymetrix, the R program I ran crashed and left
the following message:
------------------------------
terminate called after throwing an instance of
'affymetrix_calvin_exceptions::UnableToOpenFileException'
Abort
-----------------------------

Here is the story: my laptop computer is MAC. I have
41 exon arrays (HuEx-1_0-st-v2), the total file size
is about 2GB.
I first install the latest version of R (Feb 2008
version) and aroma.affymetrix, and when I run the the
following basic code:

library(aroma.affymetrix)
chipType <- "HuEx-1_0-st-v2"
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(chipType,
tags="core")
print(cdf)
BC.exon <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("BcExonArray",
cdf=cdf)
print(BC.exon)

--- When I run the above "print(BC.exon)", I got:
# > print(BC.exon)
# terminate called after throwing an instance of
'affymetrix_calvin_exceptions::UnableToO
# penFileException'
# Abort trap

But when I try only 4 arrays, it works well, so I
thought two reasons might explain this:
1) the number of arrays are too large
2) my laptop computer is not powerful

Later I switch to other powerful working stations at
berkeley stats and LBL, when I tried to use
"print(BC.exon)".
R crashed again and I got the same message again.
Later I avoided using "print(BC.exon)", and go to run
background correction
and R crashed again, I got the same message, see the
following:

bc<-RmaBackgroundCorrection(BC.exon)
system.time(process.bc<-process(bc, verbose=verbose) )

terminate called after throwing an instance of
'affymetrix_calvin_exceptions::UnableToOpenFileException'
Abort

Note: The R versions of Berkeley stats and LBL are:
2.5.1 (2007-06-27) and 2.6.0 (2007-10-03)

I guess the R version may not matter that much, this
problem might be due to the number of arrays and the
size of the exon array files.
Are there some ways I can fix it, or turn around this
problem?

Any comments and suggestions are welcome, thanks for
your attention!

Shuying

parts:
Shuying.

The number of arrays is definitely NOT too large. I have done >125
exon chips on a small computer. You should be able to run
aroma.affymetrix with very little memory (< 500Mb).

A couple quick queries:

1. Can you give the results of 'sessionInfo()' so we know exactly
what versions you are using?

2. What CDF file are you using and where did you get it from?


Mark

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: R crashed: terminate called after throwing an instance of 'affymetrix_calvin_exceptions::UnableToOpenFileException'
parts:
On Sun, Mar 30, 2008 at 10:03 PM, Mark Robinson <mrob...@wehi.edu.au> wrote:
>
> Shuying.
>
> The number of arrays is definitely NOT too large. I have done >125
> exon chips on a small computer. You should be able to run
> aroma.affymetrix with very little memory (< 500Mb).
>
> A couple quick queries:
>
> 1. Can you give the results of 'sessionInfo()' so we know exactly
> what versions you are using?
>
> 2. What CDF file are you using and where did you get it from?

Yes, it is not a memory problem or that you data set is too big.
Instead, my best guess is that you have one or more corrupted CEL
files. The crash/core dump is happening when calling affxparser
(based on Fusion SDK), which is the package used to read CEL files.
We are aware that affxparser has problems and can crash R if corrupt
files are used. We hope to add exception handling to affxparser at
some stage prevent it from crashing and instead returning a nice error
message.

To figure out what CEL file(s) might cause the problem, do this:

library(aroma.affymetrix);
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("HuEx-1_0-st-v2", tags="core");
cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName("BcExonArray", cdf=cdf);
for (kk in seq(cs)) {
cf <- getFile(cs, kk);
pathname <- getPathname(cf);
print(list(kk=kk, pathname=pathname, fi=file.info(pathname)));
print(cf);
}

Most likely this will crash when print(cf) is done on a corrupt CEL
file. This way you will be able to identify the bad CEL files and
most likely there is an obvious answer why they are corrupt.

/Henrik

guess it is due to my way of "copy and paste" files,
or due to the way I transferred files between

again from the original resources and now it seems
work well. Many thanks for your kind help!
